beats.headline: QCOM surges 15.1% after Q2 10-Q and 8-K filings
beats.explanation: Qualcomm shares jumped 15.12% to $179.58 on trading volume 4.7 times its 30-day average following the release of its quarterly 10-Q and 8-K filings the prior evening. The gain was largely company-specific, far outpacing supplier TSM (+0.57%) and customer AAPL (+0.44%), while competitors traded mixed.

beats.headline: QCOM advances 10.8% alongside competitor rally
beats.explanation: Qualcomm rose 10.79% to close at $186.55 on 2.6 times average volume without company-specific news. The advance was shared with several competitors, notably INTC, which rallied 12.91%, and AMD, which gained 4.02%.

beats.headline: QCOM gains 5.2% in company-specific advance
beats.explanation: Qualcomm climbed 5.18% to $202.55 on 3.9 times average volume despite the absence of company-specific headlines. The move was company-specific, as competitors AMD (-3.07%), AVGO (-3.03%), and INTC (-3.00%) all declined.

beats.headline: QCOM climbs 8.4% to $237.53 on heavy volume
beats.explanation: Qualcomm advanced 8.42% to close at $237.53 on volume 3.5 times the 30-day average. No company-specific filings or news accompanied the move, though competitor INTC gained 3.62% while customer AAPL edged down 0.22%.

beats.headline: QCOM drops 11.5% as peer semiconductors retreat
beats.explanation: Qualcomm fell 11.46% to $210.31 on volume 3.0 times its 30-day average. The pullback was shared across several competitors, including INTC (-6.82%), CRUS (-4.45%), and AMD (-2.29%), in the absence of Qualcomm-specific news.

beats.headline: QCOM drops 6.1% against broader semiconductor gains
beats.explanation: Qualcomm shares fell 6.14% to $200.08 on volume 1.9 times normal without company-specific news. The drop was company-specific, as supplier TSM rose 4.48% and competitors AVGO and NVDA advanced 5.52% and 4.39%, respectively.

beats.headline: QCOM rises 5.4% to $213.41 on elevated volume
beats.explanation: Qualcomm gained 5.38% to finish at $213.41 on 2.2 times average volume without company news. Competitors were largely muted or lower, including INTC (-0.39%) and NVDA (-1.77%), while customer AAPL moved up 0.91%.

beats.headline: QCOM jumps 11.6% to $238.16 as volume expands
beats.explanation: Qualcomm rose 11.60% to $238.16 with trading volume 2.3 times normal. While no direct news was reported, competitor AMD also gained 3.99% and competitor CRUS rose 2.73%, while supplier TSM slipped 0.65%.

beats.headline: QCOM falls 8.8% to $228.99 on 1.6x volume
beats.explanation: Qualcomm declined 8.78% to $228.99 without company-specific disclosures. The retreat was shared with competitor INTC (-4.67%) and customer AAPL (-1.84%), even as supplier TSM rose 4.11% and competitor NVDA climbed 6.26%.

beats.headline: QCOM gains 3.8% following Form 8-K filing
beats.explanation: Qualcomm rose 3.79% to $204.90 on 2.7 times normal volume after filing a Form 8-K the prior day. The gain occurred as competitor AMD added 2.47%, while customer AAPL dropped 6.12%.

beats.headline: QCOM slides 7.6% alongside broader peer weakness
beats.explanation: Qualcomm lost 7.57% to close at $189.39 on 2.9 times average volume. The decline was shared across competitors CRUS (-4.86%), AVGO (-3.67%), and INTC (-3.42%), even as customer AAPL gained 3.14%.

beats.headline: QCOM slides 5.8% on Apple iPhone share loss reports
beats.explanation: Qualcomm fell 5.82% to $177.72 on 4.2 times average volume following reports that its component share in customer Apple's recent iPhone launch would fall materially below its previous 20% estimate. The selloff was company-specific, as supplier TSM rose 1.02% and competitors AMD and AVGO climbed 2.70% and 2.97%, respectively.

ev_QCOM_20260918_news2.detail: Reported by Yahoo. NVIDIA (NVDA) is the strongest business in its peer group, and it is priced below every rival you can compare it with fairly, at 27.5 times earnings. Yet over the past twelve months NVDA returned 25.7% while AMD returned 239.7%. The best business in the group is one of its weakest stocks, and not because anyone doubts the demand.

ev_QCOM_20260918_news3.title: What Needs To Be True To Buy Qualcomm Stock Now?
ev_QCOM_20260918_news3.detail: Reported by Yahoo. Qualcomm (QCOM) told investors in its fiscal Q3 2026 call that its share of Apple's recent iPhone launch would be materially lower than its prior estimate of 20%. In the same call, management raised its non-handset revenue target for fiscal 2029 to $40 billion—nearly doubling its prior $22 billion goal as automotive, IoT, and data center expand. Anyone buying the stock today is deciding whether that replacement revenue arrives on schedule.

ev_QCOM_20260918_news7.title: Apple’s Chip Strategy Keeps Paying Dividends
ev_QCOM_20260918_news7.detail: Reported by Yahoo. When Apple’s iPhone turned into an immediate hit upon its 2007 release, CEO Steve Jobs was quick to realize the value of designing and owning as many of the components in its devices as possible.  Since then, designing the main chips for all its devices has been a priority for  Apple  and a potent differentiator, enabling deeper integration between software, services, and hardware than any other consumer technology company.  This week’s release of iPhone 18 Pro and the A20 Pro chip inside of it, makes the advantages of Apple’s chip strategy as clear as day.

arc: Between late April and September 2026, Qualcomm experienced extreme volatility characterized by an aggressive spring rally followed by a full unwinding of those gains. The initial surge was sparked by its Q2 financial filings on April 29, which lifted shares 15.12% and drove a momentum run that peaked near $238 in late May, frequently decoupling from peer movements. However, gains proved difficult to sustain through June amid broad semiconductor pullbacks, culminating in a sharp September selloff to $177.72 driven by confirmation that Qualcomm's component share in key customer Apple's newest iPhone fell materially below prior 20% expectations.
